stories.headline: OpenAI teams up with Hacktron
stories.body: **Partnering to hunt bugs:** OpenAI announced a collaboration with Hacktron to find vulnerabilities, test third‑party integrations, and harden its frontier AI systems.
stories.why: Knowing the threat surface helps you design safer AI pipelines.

stories.headline: Kernel patch lets hibernation survive lockdown
stories.body: **Sleep mode under lock:** Matthew Garrett submitted a patch that enables hibernation while the system is in lockdown mode, guarding against tampering and downgrade attacks.
stories.why: Your embedded devices can now power down securely without losing state.

stories.headline: Airbyte climbs GitHub trending list
stories.body: **ELT for the masses:** Airbyte’s open‑source project moves data from APIs, databases, and files into warehouses, lakes, or AI apps, available self‑hosted or in the cloud.
stories.why: Simplifies feeding fresh data into your ML models.

quick_hits.text: **Updates:** AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Oracle push dozens of security patches, including kernel and glibc.
**Xen fixes:** Seven stable kernels address three use‑after‑free bugs in Xen hypervisor.
**Robot sandbox:** ToyBlocks offers a simulated world for systematic robot learning evaluation.
**AI hub:** PipesHub adds 50+ connectors for self‑hosted enterprise knowledge search.
**Graphics debug:** RenderDoc lets you capture and inspect frames from Vulkan, DirectX, OpenGL, and more.

brief.sign_off: Catch you tomorrow—same time, same code.

highlights.title: First steps in bare-metal programming using UEFI
highlights.summary: A Hacker News post outlines initial steps for bare‑metal programming using UEFI.
highlights.detail: The guide walks developers through setting up a minimal UEFI application, compiling for a target platform, and flashing firmware, providing a practical entry point for low‑level system work without an operating system.

highlights.title: Security updates for Friday
highlights.summary: AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, and Oracle issued security updates for dozens of packages including kernel, glibc, mariadb, php, and firefox on Friday.
highlights.detail: The updates cover a wide range of components such as container-tools, gcc-toolset-12, gimp 2.8, go-toolset, libfastjson, mysql 8.0, squid 4, rust crates, and more. Each distribution lists its own affected packages, reflecting coordinated effort across Linux ecosystems to patch known vulnerabilities.

highlights.title: Partnering with Hacktron to find vulnerabilities in OpenAI’s systems
highlights.summary: OpenAI announced a partnership with Hacktron to locate vulnerabilities, test third‑party integrations, and improve defenses for frontier AI systems.
highlights.detail: The collaboration aims to combine Hacktron's security expertise with OpenAI's infrastructure, focusing on proactive threat hunting and hardening of API connections. It reflects a broader industry trend of engaging external red teams for AI safety.

highlights.title: [$] Locking down hibernation for the winter
highlights.summary: Matthew Garrett submitted a kernel patch to allow hibernation under lockdown mode while protecting against tampering and downgrade attacks.
highlights.detail: Current lockdown disables hibernation because the kernel cannot verify the integrity of the saved memory image. The proposed changes add cryptographic verification and version checks, aiming to keep the security guarantees of lockdown without sacrificing suspend-to-disk functionality.

highlights.title: airbytehq/airbyte
highlights.summary: Airbyte’s open‑source project enables ELT data movement from APIs, databases, and files to warehouses, lakes, and AI applications, available for self‑hosted or cloud deployment.
highlights.detail: The repository, written in Python, includes connectors for a wide range of sources and destinations, facilitating integration pipelines for machine‑learning workloads. Community contributions drive new adapters and improvements.

items.title: ToyBlocks: A controlled world for robot learning and evaluation
items.summary: ToyBlocks is a simulated environment designed for robot learning and systematic evaluation.
items.detail: The platform provides a controllable, physics‑based world where researchers can benchmark manipulation policies under repeatable conditions, facilitating reproducibility and rapid iteration compared to real‑world robot trials.

items.summary: The OBLITERATUS/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-obliterated model has been downloaded 2,640 times and received 269 likes on Hugging Face.
items.detail: Listed under text‑generation, the model appears to attract moderate community interest. Its popularity may indicate usefulness for downstream generation tasks, though no performance metrics are provided.

items.title: Seven stable kernels with fixes for three Xen vulnerabilities
items.summary: Seven Linux stable kernels (7.3.3, 6.18.62, 6.12.116, 6.6.162, 6.1.192, 5.15.225, 5.10.274) were released fixing three Xen use‑after‑free bugs (CVE‑2026‑100080, CVE‑2026‑100081, CVE‑2026‑100082).
items.detail: Two of the CVEs could cause a denial‑of‑service and possible information leakage on the Xen host, while the third also enables privilege escalation. Users running Xen are advised to upgrade to any of the listed stable releases.

items.title: Two stable kernels for Friday
items.summary: Greg Kroah‑Hartman released Linux stable kernels 7.3.2 and 6.18.61 on Friday, containing numerous tree‑wide changes.
items.detail: Both kernels incorporate a variety of bug fixes and minor feature updates across subsystems. The announcement encourages users to upgrade to benefit from the latest stability improvements.

items.title: Videos from XDC 2026 are available
items.summary: Videos from the 2026 X.Org Developers Conference held in Toronto (Sept 28‑30) are now posted on YouTube.
items.detail: The conference covered updates to the X Window System, driver development, and upcoming roadmap items. The recordings provide full access to talks and panels for developers who could not attend in person.

items.title: airbytehq/airbyte
items.summary: Airbyte’s open‑source project enables ELT data movement from APIs, databases, and files to warehouses, lakes, and AI applications, available for self‑hosted or cloud deployment.
items.detail: The repository, written in Python, includes connectors for a wide range of sources and destinations, facilitating integration pipelines for machine‑learning workloads. Community contributions drive new adapters and improvements.

items.title: pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-ai
items.summary: PipesHub is an open-source, self‑hosted context layer that lets AI agents search and cite a company's knowledge across Slack, Drive, Jira, GitHub, Microsoft 365 and over 50 connectors.
items.detail: It provides permission‑aware workspaces and includes MCP, SDKs, and built‑in agents for integration. The platform aims to centralize enterprise data for AI‑driven workflows without relying on external services.

items.title: antoniaci/blackbird
items.summary: Blackbird is an OSINT utility that searches social networks for accounts linked to a given username or email address.
items.detail: The tool automates enumeration across multiple platforms, helping investigators quickly map online identities. It is written in Python and available as an open‑source project.

items.title: baldurk/renderdoc
items.summary: RenderDoc is a stand‑alone graphics debugging application for capturing and inspecting frames from DirectX, Vulkan, OpenGL, and other APIs.
items.detail: Developers use it to analyze rendering pipelines, spot performance bottlenecks, and verify shader output. The tool runs on Windows, Linux, and macOS and supports a wide range of GPU hardware.

items.title: django/django
items.summary: Django is a Python web framework that emphasizes rapid development and clean, pragmatic design.
items.detail: It includes an ORM, templating engine, authentication system, and extensive admin interface, enabling developers to build scalable sites with minimal boilerplate. The project is maintained by a large open‑source community.

items.title: fmtlib/fmt
items.summary: fmt is a modern C++ formatting library offering type‑safe, Python‑style string interpolation.
items.detail: It replaces traditional printf‑style functions with compile‑time checks, improving safety and performance. The library is header‑only, supports C++20 features, and integrates with standard streams.
